svg.title: Agent Memory temporal architecture
svg.desc: Mobile-first architecture showing canonical Agent Memory state flowing through a deterministic temporal commitment, optional UOR exact identity, signer attestation and trust evidence, external timestamp or transparency evidence, separate currentness, a governed projection compatibility gate, Dogwood temporal policy or Cedar and Cedarling authorization consumers, then external policy evidence composed monotonically with PAMA. The diagram emphasizes that identity, signature validity, signer trust, witnessed time, historical truth, currentness, policy compatibility, and authority are separate claims.
svg.text: Temporal memory architecture
Preserve history, prove what can be proved, and keep present authority separate.
THE CLAIMS THAT MUST STAY SEPARATE
content identity != truth
signature validity != signer trust
witnessed existence time != event occurrence time
historical truth != current truth
policy compatibility != permission != PAMA authority
Each layer strengthens a different statement about memory.
01 CANONICAL AGENT MEMORY
Memory semantics remain here
identity · provenance · claimed / observed / validity time
scope · isolation · schema · correction · supersession
revocation · deletion · derivation · currentness · PAMA
Historical state and current applicability are both representable.
External peers strengthen or consume memory; they do not own its canonical meaning.
02 DETERMINISTIC TEMPORAL COMMITMENT
Commit the temporal meaning itself
payload / subject · event time · observed time · validity interval
scope · schema/profile · stream · sequence · predecessor
Material mutation -> different exact content identity.
The historical object remains immutable even when currentness later changes.
Tamper evidence is not truth evidence and grants no authority.
03 OPTIONAL UOR EXACT IDENTITY
Portable reference to the exact committed object
Optional first profile: UOR-Addr content addressing.
Useful for cross-runtime identity and replay references.
UOR identity != signer identity != truth != authority
04 SIGNER ATTESTATION + TRUST EVIDENCE
Two questions, two evidence layers
Key possession:
did this key sign this exact commitment?
Signer trust:
is this exact key material trusted now?
trust binds key ref + public-key digest + source + verification + validity
Valid historical signature can coexist with revoked or expired trust.
A friendly key name cannot transfer trust to different key material.
05 EXTERNAL TIME + TRANSPARENCY EVIDENCE
Independent evidence about existence and history
RFC 3161 timestamp evidence -> existed by externally verified time T
inclusion receipt -> exact subject included under declared VDS profile
consistency proof -> bounded append-only transition between tree states
Stronger history evidence remains bounded evidence.
No single receipt proves complete history or global non-equivocation.
Witnessed existence time != event occurrence time != currentness
06 CURRENTNESS + LIFECYCLE
What does this historical object mean now?
current · superseded · disputed · revoked · deleted · unknown
Currentness evidence can change without rewriting signed history.
Historical integrity != current applicability
07 GOVERNED PROJECTION + COMPATIBILITY GATE
Export the smallest truthful representation needed
versioned projection · source currentness · schema/policy identity
temporal horizon · isolation · actually evaluated context
current · migration_required · incompatible · unknown
Serializable context can still be semantically stale.
08 ALIGNED POLICY CONSUMERS
Dogwood:
bounded temporal policy over governed event/context projection
Cedar / Cedarling:
authorization and embedded PDP/runtime surfaces
External policy decisions return as evidence and compose monotonically with PAMA; external ALLOW cannot silently widen Agent Memory authority.
